photo.fileTitle: File:Hakkapeliitta Pääsiäisenä 1941-04 p461 SOTASISUA PILLERISTÄ Finnish military magazine WW2 article on German stimulant PERITIN methamphetamine as safe sisu pill banishing fatigue boosting soldiers endurance and morale PD.jpg
photo.caption: Article in the Finnish military magazine Hakkapeliitta (April 1941) praising the new German stimulant Pervitin (methamphetamine hydrochloride) as a safe sisu pill that banishes fatigue and boosts soldiers’ endurance and morale. At the time, Finland cooperated with Nazi Germany during World War II.
photo.description: Uncredited article from the Finnish national defense magazine Hakkapeliitta, published in April 1941. Hakkapeliitta was the weekly magazine (1925–1944) of the Finnish voluntary Home Guard organization, known in English as the White Guard (Finnish: Suojeluskunnat), a paramilitary organization formed leading up to the Finnish Civil War in 1918. The organization and its publication were abolished in 1944. photo.fileTitle: File:Rational harm assessment of drugs radar plot.svg
photo.caption: Addiction experts in psychiatry, chemistry, pharmacology, forensic science, epidemiology, and the police and legal services engaged in delphic analysis regarding 20 popular recreational drugs. Amphetamine was ranked 8th in dependence, 6th in physical harm, and 9th in social harm.
photo.description: Radar plot depicting the data presented in Nutt, David, Leslie A King, William Saulsbury, Colin Blakemore. "Development of a rational scale to assess the harm of drugs of potential misuse" The Lancet 2007; 369:1047-1053. PMID:17382831. For more information, see image. It contains not only the physical harm and dependence data like the aforementioned image, but also the mean social harm of each drug. This image was produced with the python plotting library matplotlib. This image is a reproduction of this image originally in png format.
